stage: reduce budgeted scheduler control-path overhead while preserving cyclic fairness and global budgets
implementation: Replace the per-action availability array/modulo-index scan with direct branches implementing the same three cyclic orders0/1/2,1/2/0,2/0/1. Turn updates still occur once per selected action and retain fairness across poll boundaries.

Do not clear LastIssue immediately before overwriting it from an eager query result. Every terminal/pending/fallback path still publishes a complete issue value and HasNext state; future faults and physical leases retain the previous contract.

Global traversal budgets, WorkLimit, FIFO quanta, reserved query credit, no-progress rotation, provisional admission, output credits, clock/ownership/error semantics are unchanged. No new state, allocation, lock, callback, dependency or shared runtime.
costs: Removed the per-action temporary array/index loop and modulo3 arithmetic; generated GCC prologues reserve16 fewer stack bytes on both tested x64 platforms. Reservation excludes register pushes/callees, not a whole-call maximum stack claim.

Final complete-function static disassembly counts are Windows700 to693 and WSL673 to679; branch/code placement can grow other paths. Static instruction counts are not executed instruction counts or a cycle/speedup guarantee.

Existing416-byte query reserve/job,240-byte hot slot, kernel/service storage, API validation/output copies, zone/calendar work, queue/heap operations and40-byte service LastPoll publication remain real costs. No zero-overhead claim.
verification: Both platforms pass19 full modular/single programs, the runnable scheduler example and static/shared real consumers. Existing184320 policy-model samples per scheduler program remain; no benchmark-only fast path or weakened test is introduced.

Global work/zero-output/sparse query/admission rollback, live-owner clock-credit barriers and Capacity1/WorkLimit3 starvation regression all run on final bytes.128 sparse lifecycles and more than10000 true resumptions retain OOM/error/allocation/lifetime coverage.

WSL O2 ASan/UBSan/leak-halt plus four O1 TSan scheduler/service modular/single units pass. Windows79 tooling tests and feature/single/reference/docs checks pass. Public/private declarations are unchanged; no new ABI claim is inferred from benchmark results.

build_recipe.source:
import os,sys,json,subprocess,hashlib
from pathlib import Path
root=Path.cwd();out=root/'out/service-extensions/xcron-budget-hotpath';phase=sys.argv[1]
assert phase in ('before','after','prototype')
mode='windows' if os.name=='nt' else 'wsl';arch='native' if os.name=='nt' else 'x64';platform='windows' if os.name=='nt' else 'linux';suffix='.exe' if os.name=='nt' else ''
sys.path.insert(0,str(root/'tools'));import build
commands=[];original=build._run_compiler
def compiler(cmd,*a,**k):commands.append(cmd);return original(cmd,*a,**k)
build._run_compiler=compiler;cc=build._compiler('gcc');overlay=build.expand_manifest_paths([Path('extlibs/xcron/config/modules.json')])
sources,tests,single,examples,defines,links,mods,byname,includes,headers=build._load_modules('xcron_scheduler',overlay,platform=platform)
flags=['-O2','-I',str(root)]
for p in includes:flags+=['-I',str(root/p)]
sha=lambda p:hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
files={root/p for p in sources}
for p in headers:
 p=root/p
 files.update(p.rglob('*.h') if p.is_dir() else [p])
files.update([root/'extlibs/xcron/bench/bench_scheduler.c',root/'extlibs/xcron/bench/bench_scheduler_budgeted.c',out/'bulk_probe.c'])
source_inputs={str(p.relative_to(root)).replace('\\','/'):sha(p) for p in sorted(files)}
objects=build._compile_objects(cc,arch,sources,defines,out/(mode+'-'+phase+'-obj'),True,flags,headers,platform)
bins={}
for name,source in [('sync','extlibs/xcron/bench/bench_scheduler.c'),('budgeted','extlibs/xcron/bench/bench_scheduler_budgeted.c'),('bulk',str((out/'bulk_probe.c').relative_to(root)))]:
 exe=out/(mode+'-'+phase+'-'+name+suffix)
 build._compile_program(cc,arch,source,objects,defines,links,exe,flags,[],platform)
 bins[name]=dict(path=str(exe),sha256=sha(exe))
dump=str(Path(cc).with_name('objdump.exe')) if mode=='windows' else 'objdump'
assembly=out/(mode+'-'+phase+'-poll.asm')
with assembly.open('w') as f:subprocess.run([dump,'-d','--disassemble=xcronSchedulerPollBudgeted',bins['budgeted']['path']],stdout=f,check=True)
assert all(sha(root/p)==h for p,h in source_inputs.items())
(out/(mode+'-'+phase+'-build.json')).write_text(json.dumps(dict(commands=commands,inputs=source_inputs,binaries=bins,assembly_sha256=sha(assembly)),indent=2)+'\n')
print(mode,phase,'compiled',flush=True)

supplemental_probe.explanation: Bulk diagnostic removes per-batch wall-clock reads AND sample-array allocation/writes; it keeps actual kernel Poll, successor advancement and Complete. Windows reads QueryThreadCycleTime twice per full run; Linux reads CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID. It has no latency/P99 claim, executes no worker/body, and cannot attribute differences to timers alone.

performance_limits: Existing four profiles, compiler flags, benchmark sources and5% throughput/10% P99 and MAD3%/central-range6% gates are unchanged. Official baseline/current benchmark fingerprints match naturally; original reports are not rewritten or forced.

Unpinned formal checks remain the original qualification path. Both platform reports and all previous failed samples remain evidence; favorable pinned/bulk diagnostics do not replace or waive a failed formal gate.

Raw formal medians also breach original thresholds: budgeted1-job throughput Windows4.632M versus5.497M/s and WSL5.026M versus6.981M/s; WSL budgeted128-job P99 23.8 versus20.1us, plus several synchronous controls. formal_median_failures enumerates every breach even though the original runner stops at its failed noise gate.

Controlled original-benchmark probes run archived ee3a125a pre-budget binaries, f64a1bad synchronous/budgeted binaries and current synchronous/budgeted binaries in five alternating repetitions with every warmup/sample retained and equal checksums.

Pinned diagnostics change only their own process affinity toCPU4 and increase original1/128-job batches to1M/100K. The default unpinned probes retain200K/10K. These count/affinity differences are explicit and cannot be compared as one production acceptance run.

Windows actual QPC frequency10MHz gives a nominal0.1us tick; recorded single-job0.2/0.3us P99 values are coarse, but every threshold breach remains a failure. Neither quantization nor background load grants a pass.

Bulk CPU units are Windows thread cycles versus Linux thread CPU nanoseconds, not cross-platform comparable. Unchanged synchronous controls are retained to expose environment/code-placement variation; improvements are observations, not isolated causal proof.

Current WSL original1-job budgeted/before ratios0.94125 unpinned and0.92797 pinned breach5%; unpinned128-job P99 ratio1.10965 breaches10%. A targeted three-binary1M single-job isolation does not reproduce a second-edit slowdown (prototype1.00098 and both1.02222 versus before), but does not waive or erase any failed sample or identify its root cause.

Other work was observed compiling locally on Windows/WSL; its files/processes/settings were preserved. Native Linux, deployment isolation, mixed/adversarial loads, full service tail latency, CPU/power and>=72h production acceptance remain open.
remaining: Retain all unresolved original performance gates and validate under qualified native deployment conditions; this local control-path improvement does not complete performance acceptance.
Continue named database/reload, nominal gap/fold delivery, durable recovery and original Redis/RPC/MQTT scope. All four libraries remain in development.
setup: Initial supplemental build recipe treated header-root directories as files and failed before compilation; it was corrected and original setup logs are retained. No product code change was required.
